_comment: bb-auth settings file — TEMPLATE. The real one is <install-dir>/var/lib/settings.json,
created by the package and never shipped, exactly like access.json: it is state.
What is in here and what is not is decided by one rule. A setting lives in this file
iff it (1) is read per request, so a new value takes effect on the next one, (2) cannot
lock the operator out if it is wrong, and (3) is not a secret. Everything else stays in
bb-auth.env, on the host: the listener, the worker count, the HMAC key, the Cognito
trust roots, the cookie's name and domain, BB_AUTH_LOGIN_URL, BB_AUTH_AUTHORIZED_HOSTS
and BB_AUTH_ORIGINAL_URL_HEADER.
It is a file rather than more env vars for one mechanical reason: a process cannot
re-read its own environment. systemd loads EnvironmentFile= once, at ExecStart, so
nothing in an env file can ever be reloaded without a restart.
Edit it with `bb-auth-adm settings ...`, or from bb-auth-web's Settings tab; both go
through the same validate-before-write. Check one by hand with:
bb-auth --check-settings settings.json
The gate re-reads it on SIGHUP (systemctl reload bb-auth) and a file it refuses leaves
the running values in place; bb-auth-web reads it fresh on every request.
COMMENTS LIVE UP HERE, and that is not a limitation to work around: unknown keys inside
a section are a hard error, for the reason a misspelled scope field is one. A setting
silently dropped is worse than a setting refused. Unknown keys at THIS level are kept
across an edit, which is what makes these blocks survive a save from either editor.
_comment_profile_claims: gate.profile_claims — OIDC claims to hand to the application on a 204, in the order the
headers come out. EMPTY BY DEFAULT: nothing is propagated but the identity.
The header name is DERIVED and never configured: '_' and ':' become '-', each part is
title-cased, and 'X-Auth-' is prefixed. given_name -> X-Auth-Given-Name,
$upstream_http_x_auth_custom_department). A claim name may contain only [A-Za-z0-9_:-];
anything else, a claim the gate consumes itself (email, email_verified, token_use,
identities), or two entries deriving the same header, is refused rather than skipped.
These are self-asserted profile attributes: display hints, never authorization. They
ride inside the session cookie, so keep the list short (a browser silently drops a
cookie over ~4 KB, and the gate warns at startup when you get close). Changing it is NOT
a cookie-format change: nobody is logged out, a claim removed stops being emitted at
once, and one added appears at each user's next sign-in.
_comment_identity_attrs: gate.identity_attrs — which identity attributes a 204 names. Default ['email'], which is
what every application behind the gate already reads. Only 'email' and 'uuid' exist; a
third would be a code change, not a string you may invent. An empty list is refused: a
204 that names nobody breaks every application behind the gate, in silence.
NGINX MUST CLEAR EVERY POSSIBLE NAME, not the ones enabled here. proxy_set_header
overrides only the names it lists, so a header you neither set nor clear is one a client
can send. Clear X-Auth-Uuid on every gated location even while it is off, and turning it
on here later needs no nginx change at all.
Multiple values of one attribute come out SPACE-separated (a user with two emails); a
space can never appear inside an identifier, which is what makes that unambiguous.
_comment_social: gate.allow_unverified_social — relax the email_verified requirement, but ONLY for
federated (social) logins. Cognito cannot verify the email of a Google/Apple sign-up, so
it stamps email_verified=false even though the IdP asserted the address. Native
self-signup stays strict: an unverified native email is attacker-controlled. It
multiplies with an 'authenticated' scope: together they mean any social account,
gate.social_providers narrows it to named IdPs, matched case-insensitively against the
token's identities[].providerName. Empty = any federated provider. Prefer listing only
_comment_session_ttl_secs: gate.session_ttl_secs — the session cookie's lifetime, in seconds. Applies to cookies
minted from now on and to no cookie already in a browser, so changing it logs nobody
out. Below 60s is refused (a session that expires as it is handed over is a login loop);
above 400 days is warned about, because that is the cap browsers apply to Max-Age
regardless of what the header says.
_comment_admins: web.admins — who may use bb-auth-web, matched against the X-Auth-Email nginx injects
(trimmed and lowercased, so a login's capitalisation cannot matter). REQUIRED and never
empty: bb-auth-web refuses to serve without one, and both editors refuse to write an
empty list. The gate ignores this section entirely.
It is deliberate defense in depth, not a second copy of the roster: a scope that grants
on identity alone (anonymous or authenticated) covering the admin URL would otherwise
hand the admin surface to any Cognito account, and self-signup is open. But it is the
BACKSTOP, not the lock: the gate is what stands in front, so the admin area must be a
'restricted' scope that lists each admin, and covered by NO anonymous or authenticated
The GUI will not let an administrator remove themselves from this list. That is on
purpose, and `bb-auth-adm settings admin rm` is the way to do it anyway.
